author: DailyMail
title: Police Officer Attacked with Crowbar During London Gang Crackdown
text:
A police officer was hit in the face with a crowbar while arresting a suspected drug dealer during Operation Gallium, a week-long Metropolitan Police crackdown that led to 297 arrests and 38 weapons seized.
A heroic police officer was attacked with a crowbar while arresting a suspected drug dealer during a week-long Metropolitan Police crackdown on gang violence in South London.
The officer and a plainclothes colleague stopped a 28-year-old man riding a stolen moped in Brixton. Tied to the moped was a carrier bag containing MDMA, cocaine and pink cocaine - a popular cocktail of ketamine, MDMA and caffeine mixed with pink food dye. Cannabis and £1,500 in cash were also discovered. When the man ran away, the officers chased and cornered him in a car park.
During the struggle, he struck one officer in the face with the crowbar and was then subdued and arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply and grievous bodily harm. He has since been bailed pending further enquiries. The incident happened during Operation Gallium, a coordinated push to tackle gun crime and serious violence across Lambeth and Southwark.
That operation resulted in 297 arrests, with 238 charges including possession of dangerous weapons, possession and supply of Class A drugs, and attempted murder. Two hundred and thirty-three stop and searches were carried out, leading to 40 arrests. Thirteen weapons sweeps contributed to the seizure of 38 dangerous weapons, including knives and firearms. The crackdown was mounted because of a rise in gang-related tensions and a series of high-profile violent incidents in recent months.
Officers executed warrants, conducted stop and searches to remove dangerous drugs and weapons from the streets, and apprehended known gang members who had contributed to rising serious youth violence in the area. Alongside the moped arrest, officers saw another suspect discard a bag containing Class A drugs while being chased. The week-long operation involved both plainclothes officers and armed response units deployed to track down offenders known for carrying weapons and dealing drugs.
The force said that over the past 18 months, the number of the most serious violent offences has fallen by almost 20 per cent, with knife crime down by 18 per cent in both boroughs in the year to June 30. However, gun crime has risen by 5 per cent in Lambeth and 11 per cent in Southwark. The action came after several recent tragedies.
Abdulkadir Mahamed, 22, was fatally stabbed on Tremadoc Road, Clapham, on July 25; Javed Khan, 22, from Wandsworth, has been charged with murder and violent disorder. On the same day, a masked motorist pointed a gun at a man outside a Cost Cutter in Thessaly Road, Vauxhall; the firearm is believed to have jammed before the suspect fled. Three men have also been charged with the murder of Kamahl Cameron-Williams, 31, on Westow Hill in Crystal Palace on June 21.
Keanu Taylor, 25, was attending a barbecue on Coldharbour Lane, Brixton, when he was wounded in a drive-by shooting on May 2 and died two days later. Detective Chief Superintendent Emma Bond, who led Operation Gallium, said: 'This activity is part of an ongoing campaign to drive down violence and make our neighbourhoods safer. That sustained approach is already delivering results, with knife crime down by 18 per cent across Lambeth and Southwark.
But we know that despite this success, gangs continue to do harm to London's communities. In recent weeks and months, more families have had to endure the unimaginable pain of losing a loved one to senseless violence. We do not want to see another life lost, which is why we're so determined to keep taking robust action. Those driving serious violence across London should be under no illusion.
We are targeting them relentlessly, and we will use every power available to take weapons, drugs and dangerous offenders off our streets.
